header: The synthesis model is shown each source as "[Circular id=49] Title: ...". That id is the database's internal row number: it means nothing to a reader (the archive shows the circular as 007, the document prints 2026/51), yet the model sometimes copies it into its own wording ("Corrected amount per Circular 49"). A prompt rule asks it not to, but THIS is my guarantee: any reference to a known source id is replaced by that circular's archive label ("Circular 007 (2026)": the number the circulars modal shows, plus the year), or by its quoted title if the serial number is not known, in every text field, before anything else looks at the output. I touch only ids that really are sources of THIS answer. A printed circular number ("Circular No. 2026/51", "Circular 2026/50") and an unrelated number ("49 employees", "Circular 5" where 5 is not a source) are left alone.

symbols.name: quotedTitle
doc: Names a circular by its title; I use this only when its serial number and year are not known.

symbols.name: buildSourceNames
symbols.sig: export function buildSourceNames( citations: Array<{ id: number; headline: string }>, labels?: Map<number, string>,): Map<number, string>
doc: Maps id -> the words a reader should see: the circular's label ("Circular 007 (2026)") if known, else its quoted title.

symbols.name: NUM
doc: An id never starts with 0, so "Circular 007" (a serial number) is NOT read as the id 7. This also keeps my clean-up idempotent.

symbols.name: REF
doc: The spellings I catch: "Circular 49", "circular #49", "Circular no. 49", "Circulars 49 and 51", "Circular id=49", "[Circular id=49]", "Circular 49 (2026)"

symbols.name: replaceSourceIds
symbols.sig: export function replaceSourceIds(text: string, names: Map<number, string>): string

symbols.name: sanitizeSourceRefs
symbols.sig: export function sanitizeSourceRefs<T>(value: T, names: Map<number, string>): T
doc: Every string in a result, however deeply nested, goes through replaceSourceIds. I leave numbers (the real source ids in `sources`) untouched.

behaviours: circularLabel: serial 7 of 2026 -> 'Circular 007 (2026)' (three digits, like the circulars modal)
circularLabel: no serial, no year or nonsense -> null (never '000')
'Corrected amount per Circular 49' -> 'Corrected amount per Circular 007 (2026)'
the internal id is gone and the serial number is there
circular #49 / Circular no. 49 / circular number 49 / Circular id=49 / Circular id 49 / [Circular id=49] / CIRCULAR 49
a year the model already wrote is not doubled: 'Circular 49 (2026)'
two sources: 'Circulars 49 and 51' and 'Circulars 49, 51'
a parenthetical id disappears: 'amount (id 49) is' and 'Rates (ids=49, 51) apply.'
no serial known -> the quoted title is used instead (never the id)
a long title is shortened with an ellipsis
'Circular 007 (2026)' is a SERIAL, not the id 7: left alone even though a source has id 7
running the clean-up twice gives the same text as once (idempotent)
'Circular 7' IS the id 7 (a real source) and is replaced by ITS label, not by 49's
a PRINTED circular number is left alone: 'Circular No. 2026/51', 'Circular 2026/50', 'Circular 49/2026'
a number that is not a source is left alone: 'Circular 5', 'Circulars 12 and 13'
a source id outside the 'Circular' wording is left alone: '49 employees', 'Rs. 49', 'page 51'
text with no reference, empty text and an empty source list are safe
a mixed list keeps the unknown id: 'Circulars 49 and 12'
every nested string is cleaned; the numeric source ids in 'sources' and the values are untouched
builder: the card now reads 'Corrected amount per Circular 007 (2026)' and no internal id appears anywhere
builder: the finding that mentioned 'Circular 49' SURVIVES (it would be dropped as an ungrounded number if cleaned too late)
builder: the real figures and the citation are intact
